evidence: evolve.py's landscape model on two squares of the design surface, with soil creep and with ground that fails where it is steeper than 35 degrees, and the placement the design holds: rock set down on freshly worn ground round where it came to rest, about 86% of it within 20 km, in two readings: shared in proportion to the wear, or offered so and taken only up to what each cell lost. Each cell is 1.9 km, so where on a slope the carriers set the rock is below what the model sees, and the returned rock wears and fails as the ground does. The shares the carriers reach are the study's for lakes whose rivers bring sand. Not validated.
reading_rule: regions: for each region under the water the design gives it, each reading of the placement (shared_by_wear, no_more_than_it_lost) and each case (the share of the rock reached, the longer range, loose ground failing at 30 degrees), at each year: evolve.py's measures; heights, the spread of the ground over height; by_where_it_stood, the change of the ground that was crest, floor or between on the starting map, and of the steepest quarter; summits, the change of the thirty highest summits; the change of the rims of the largest hollows; change_m, the change of the ground by share of the land; the shares risen over 100, 300 and 1,000 m; the share of the land within two degrees of the failing slope; rock, km3. checks: grain, one crater's surroundings in the southern highlands on the design surface's cells and on cells half their size; step, the southern highlands with half the time step.
